newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Oilseeds - S.Korean millers seek price rises.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - S.Korean millers seek price rises.

text.p: South Korean feed millers have asked the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation for clearance to raise feed prices in the domestic market due to strong gains in world soymeal prices, traders said on Monday.
"Domestic feed prices are expected to rise four to five percent soon due to local producers' demand," a trader with a major feed milling company said.
He said the millers had hoped the increases would be implemented by May 1, but this was viewed as too soon and they were unlikely to go ahead before June 1.
He added that the sharp fall of the won against the U.S. dollar had prompted the millers to seek relief from heavy foreign exchange losses.
The won has plunged by more than five percent since late January to around 895 won to the dollar.
Dealers said several South Korean feed millers are still seen in the market this week despite the difficult domestic situation.
South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) has invited tenders to buy 50,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellet and 30,000 tonnes of wheat bran pellet or rice bran pellet on Friday.
In Japan, soybean traders said they will probably be sidelined this week, after covering their nearby requirements, because of the Golden Week holiday season.
U.S. Gulf/Japan freight rates are seen at just below U$22 a tonne, the dealers said.
